title: Mechanistic study of plastic monomers in gestational diabetes mellitus: A network toxicology and molecular docking approach.
one_liner_zh: 该研究用网络毒理学和分子对接探讨塑料单体与妊娠糖尿病靶蛋白的结合，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA研究无关。
abstract: Plastics are widely used in various fields such as food packaging, textile fibers, building materials, and transportation. Although the relationship between plastic additives and diseases has been reported, there is limited research on the association between plastic monomers (PM) and gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study aims to investigate the link between environmental PM and GDM. By employing advanced network toxicology and molecular docking techniques, we successfully elucidated the molecular mechanisms by which PM may induce GDM. Utilizing databases such as PubChem, SEA, Super-PRED, SwissTargetPrediction, PharmMapper, Gene Cards, and OMIM, we identified potential targets associated with the disease. Further analysis using STRING and Cytoscape software helped determine the core targets most significantly related to these metabolic disorders. Additionally, Gene Ontology and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment analyses were conducted using the David database to characterize these core targets. Finally, molecular docking with CB-Dock2 was used to validate the binding affinity of PM to these target proteins. Our findings suggest that PM may potentially induce GDM by modulating the insulin signaling pathway through STAT3, AKT1, and TP53. In summary, this work provides novel insights into the mechanisms by which environmental pollutants may trigger GDM, thereby laying a theoretical foundation for disease prevention and treatment. It offers valuable references for the safety evaluation of plastics, urging food safety regulatory agencies to strengthen oversight and encouraging the public to reduce plastic usage.
abstract_zh: 塑料在食品包装、纺织纤维、建筑材料和交通运输等多个领域被广泛使用。尽管已有关于塑料添加剂与疾病关联的报道，但关于塑料单体（PM）与妊娠期糖尿病（GDM）之间关系的研究仍有限。本研究旨在探讨环境中的PM与GDM之间的关联。通过采用先进的网络毒理学和分子对接技术，我们成功阐明了PM可能诱发GDM的分子机制。利用PubChem、SEA、Super-PRED、SwissTargetPrediction、PharmMapper、Gene Cards和OMIM等数据库，我们识别了与该疾病相关的潜在靶点。进一步使用STRING和Cytoscape软件进行分析，帮助确定了与这些代谢紊乱最显著相关的核心靶点。此外，利用David数据库进行了基因本体论和京都基因与基因组百科全书通路富集分析，以表征这些核心靶点。最后，使用CB-Dock2进行分子对接，验证了PM与这些靶蛋白的结合亲和力。我们的研究结果表明，PM可能通过STAT3、AKT1和TP53调节胰岛素信号通路，从而潜在诱发GDM。总之，这项工作为环境污染物可能触发GDM的机制提供了新的见解，从而为疾病预防和治疗奠定了理论基础。它为塑料的安全性评估提供了宝贵参考，敦促食品安全监管机构加强监督，并鼓励公众减少塑料使用。
